webex-realtime-dlp-flow.statement: Adding Webex Teams as a SaaS application tenant allows the Zscaler service to act as a smart host where Webex Teams can send messages and files for content inspection. Webex Teams messages are managed by web DLP policies and file attachments by Data at Rest Scanning DLP policies, which need SaaS Security scan schedules to inspect content; logs for messages that triggered inline DLP rules are in the Web Insights Logs for Webex, and logs for files that triggered the real-time SaaS Security DLP rules are in the SaaS Security Insights Logs page for Webex.

quotes: Adding Webex Teams as a SaaS application tenant allows the Zscaler service to act as a smart host where Webex Teams can send messages and files for content inspection.
Webex Teams messages are managed by configuring web DLP policies, while file attachments are managed by configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP policies.
In order for the Data at Rest Scanning DLP policies to inspect content in sanctioned SaaS applications, you must create SaaS Security scan schedules.

You can view the logs for messages that triggered the inline DLP rules in the Web Insights Logs for Webex and you can view the logs for files that triggered the real-time SaaS Security DLP rules in the SaaS Security Insights Logs page for Webex.

public-cloud-enablement.statement: Amazon S3, Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure are enabled for an organization by contacting the Zscaler Account team.

quotes: To enable Amazon S3, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure for your organization, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To enable Amazon S3, Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure for your organization, contact your Zscaler Account team.

tenant-authorizes-app.statement: Zscaler Data at Rest Scanning provides visibility and security for the sanctioned SaaS applications used in the organization, and a SaaS application is authorized with Zscaler by adding it as a tenant.

quotes: Zscaler Data at Rest Scanning provides visibility and security for sanctioned SaaS applications used in your organization.
You can authorize sanctioned SaaS applications with Zscaler by adding them as tenants.

tenant-name-unique.statement: A tenant name must be unique, and it is the name shown when configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP policy, the Malware Detection policy, Workflow Automation or Scan Configuration.

quotes: Enter a unique name for the SaaS application tenant.
This name is displayed when configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP policy, Malware Detection policy, Workflow Automation, or Scan Configuration

onboarding-features.statement: When adding a tenant the administrator selects the functionality to enable, from App Governance, DLP and Malware scanning SaaS API, SSPM Scan, or Workflow Automation, where the application supports it. The /casbTenant/lite filterByFeature parameter filters tenants by feature: CASB, WORKFLOW_AUTOMATION, SSPM, ACTIVITY_REPORT, TP_APP_REPORT, RT_DLP, APP_GOVERNANCE, REDACTION and CASB_ENTITY_GROUP.

quotes: Select the checkbox for the functionality you want to enable. You can choose from App Governance, DLP and Malware scanning SaaS API, SSPM Scan, or Workflow Automation if the app supports the functionality.

expect.description: Filters the SaaS application tenant by feature

tenant-states.statement: The console shows a tenant as Active (policies are enforced), Inactive (policies are not enforced), Validation Failed (the admin credentials could not be validated or the application authorized) or Reauthorization Required.

quotes: Active: The tenant is in use. Policies are enforced for this SaaS application.
Inactive: The tenant is not in use. Policies are not enforced for this SaaS application.
Validation Failed: There were issues validating the admin credentials and authorizing the SaaS application.
Reauthorization Required: The access to the application has expired. To give Zscaler access, edit the tenant

reauthorize-procedure.statement: A tenant in Reauthorization Required is fixed by editing the tenant, going to Register and Authorize, and choosing Reauthorize, which logs in to the SaaS application and gives Zscaler access again; reauthorizing GitHub also requires revoking the existing Zscaler OAuth application authorization in the GitHub portal.

quotes: Reauthorization Required: The access to the application has expired. To give Zscaler access, edit the tenant, and go to Register and Authorize, then click Reauthorize to log in to the SaaS application and give access to the tenant.
If you're reauthorizing GitHub, you must revoke the existing Zscaler OAuth application authorization in the GitHub portal.

reauth-flag.statement: A tenant record carries a boolean `reAuth`, documented by the Terraform provider as enabling tenant re-authentication, and a `lastTenantValidationTime`.

quotes: * `re_auth` - (Boolean) Enable tenant re-authentication
* `last_tenant_validation_time` - (Number) Last time the tenant was validated
ReAuth                   bool           `json:"reAuth,omitempty"`
LastTenantValidationTime int `json:"lastTenantValidationTime,omitempty"`

validate-status-states.statement: The tenant validation status endpoint returns a list of states that includes CASB_TENANT_NORMAL_RETHORIZATION and CASB_TENANT_CONNECTOR_RETHORIZATION alongside the active, inactive and validation states, with an error code and message for a failed validation.

validate-status-carries-authorization-in.statement: The validation status response also carries a `tenantAuthorizationInfo` object whose members include credential fields such as `accessToken`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `botToken` and `credJson`.

expect.description: The access token issued to the SaaS tenant application by the authorization serverfor tenant authorization

tenant-limit-16.statement: Up to 16 tenants can be added for each sanctioned SaaS application; Zscaler Support can be asked for an increase.

quotes: Up to 16 tenants can be added for each sanctioned SaaS application. Contact Zscaler Support for a possible increase in this limit.

trusted-profile-limit-32.statement: Up to 32 external trusted domain and user profiles can be added for each sanctioned SaaS application.

quotes: | Number of external trusted domain and user profiles per application | 32 profiles |
Up to 32 profiles can be added for each sanctioned SaaS application.

trusted-profiles-email-only.statement: External trusted domain profiles and external trusted user profiles apply only to email SaaS application tenants.

quotes: Displays the total number of added external trusted domains. Click to view a list of the domains. This only applies to email SaaS application tenants.
Displays the total number of added external trusted users. Click to view a list of the users. This only applies to email SaaS application tenants.

trusted-treated-internal.statement: For an Exchange tenant, the Zscaler service treats email addresses from the added external trusted domains as trusted, internal users.

quotes: The Zscaler service views any email addresses from the added domains as trusted, internal users for Exchange.

owner-zia-or-zdx.statement: A tenant records whether it was created in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) or Digital Experience (ZDX); a tenant created in ZDX cannot be deleted in ZIA, and edits in ZIA to such a tenant are allowed on any field except those relating to Workflow Automation.

quotes: Owner: Indicates whether the SaaS application tenant was created in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) or Digital Experience (ZDX).
If the tenant was created in ZDX, the delete functionality is removed in Internet & SaaS.
Edits in Internet & SaaS for tenants created in ZDX are allowed on any fields except those relating to Workflow Automation.

onboarding-quarantine-location.statement: Choosing DLP and Malware Scanning SaaS API at onboarding asks for a DLP Quarantine Location (a folder path or URL for relocated files) and a DLP Admin Email ID for supported file share applications.

quotes: If you selected DLP and Malware Scanning SaaS API for onboarding, you need to specify your quarantine location for supported file share applications.
enter a valid folder path or URL of the designated quarantine location for relocating the files
Under DLP Admin Email ID, enter the admin email address for the application.
Under DLP Quarantine Location (optional), enter a valid folder path or URL

webhook-flag.statement: The Go SDK's tenant struct carries a boolean `tenantWebhookEnabled`, documented by the Terraform provider as whether the tenant webhook feature is enabled.

quotes: (Boolean) If the tenant webhook feature is enabled
TenantWebhookEnabled     bool           `json:"tenantWebhookEnabled,omitempty"`

webex-realtime-dlp.statement: For a Webex Teams tenant both onboarding options allow rules for messages, but file attachments need the tenant onboarded for Real-time DLP, and DLP and Malware scanning SaaS API and Real-time DLP cannot be enabled at the same time for the tenant.

quotes: Both onboarding options for Webex Teams allow you to configure rules for messages, but for file attachments you need to onboard the tenant for Real-time DLP.
DLP and Malware scanning SaaS API and Real-time DLP cannot be enabled at the same time.

no-create-endpoint.statement: The ZIA OpenAPI document defines only GET operations for CASB tenants (list, scan info, validation status and policy tags), and the Terraform provider exposes the tenant only as a read-only data source, so a tenant cannot be created through the documented API.
no-create-endpoint.conditions: Rests on absence: the `/casbTenant` paths in the ZIA OpenAPI document were searched and carry only `get`; an undocumented create call is not ruled out.

expect.description: Retrieves information about the SaaS application tenant. .

quotes: data source to get information about a ZIA SaaS Application Tenants

validation-error-codes.statement: The tenant validation error codes page lists: 1 and 500, an internal error (retry after a few minutes); 2, validation timed out or was interrupted, with at least one minute needed to validate a tenant; 4, the service is unable to validate the tenant, possibly because of an ongoing release upgrade or a network issue; 201 - 299, serialization of the JSON response failed; 400 - 499, an error authenticating or authorizing the SaaS application (check that the Enterprise ID is valid and the right permissions were given); and 501 - 599, an internal server error from the SaaS application provider. Each says to contact Zscaler Support if the error persists.

quotes: 1 | An internal error occurred. | Retry validating the tenant after a few minutes. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support.

2 | The tenant validation timed out or was interrupted. It takes at least one minute to validate a tenant. | Retry validating the tenant after a few minutes. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support.

4 | The Zscaler service is unable to validate the tenant. This error might occur because there's an ongoing release upgrade or a network issue. | Retry validating the tenant later. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support.
201 - 299 | The serialization of the JSON response failed. | Retry validating the tenant later. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support.

400 - 499 | An error occurred when authenticating or authorizing the SaaS application. | Check if the Enterprise ID is valid and you gave the Zscaler service the right permissions to authorize the SaaS application. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support.
500 | An internal error occurred. | Retry validating the tenant after a few minutes. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support.
501 - 599 | An internal server error occurred from the SaaS application provider. | Retry validating the tenant later. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support.

servicenow-object-types.statement: For a ServiceNow tenant the service provides a default list of the most commonly used object types and more can be added; the Default Object Types are those that can be scanned with the Data at Rest Scanning DLP policy. For the additional object types included, the policy scans only the fields specific to description, short_description and close_notes.

quotes: ServiceNow has many object types available, so the Zscaler service provides a default list of the most commonly used object types. You can add additional object types if they're not on the list.
Default Object Types: View the default list of ServiceNow object types that you can scan with the Data at Rest Scanning Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy.
More Object Types: Enter the object types and click Add Items to include them for scanning.
For the additional object types that are included, the policy scans only the fields specific to description, short_description, and close_notes.

component-groups.statement: For SaaS applications with many component sites, such as SharePoint, groups of sites that share the same DLP policies can be created instead of a policy per site. A group is created under a SaaS Application Tenant and can contain a maximum of 10,000 sites, added manually with Add Sites (select the desired sites from a drop-down list and click Done) or with Import Sites from a CSV file. The Manage Groups tab edits or deletes existing groups, and the Manage Components tab lists all sites, tenants and site types by group, with site type available only for sites linked to a group.

quotes: SaaS applications, such as SharePoint, might have dozens, hundreds, or even thousands of individual component sites.
Instead of creating Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies for each of them individually, you can create groups of sites that you want to share the same DLP policies.
In the Add Group drawer, enter the following: - Name: The name of your group. - SaaS Application Tenant: Select one of your tenants.
A group can contain a maximum of 10,000 sites.
- Sites: Choose to manually add or import sites.
Add Sites: Click the drop-down menu, select your desired sites from the list, and click Done.
Import Sites: Click Choose File and select a CSV file with your list of desired sites.
On the Manage Groups tab, you can click the Edit or Delete icon to make any changes to an existing group.
On the Manage Components tab, you can view a list of all your sites, tenants, and site types based on the group they are associated with.
The site type is available only for those sites that are linked to a group.

not-a-tenant-profile.statement: A CASB tenant is not a Tenant Profile: tenants are chosen when configuring the Data at Rest Scanning DLP policy, the Malware Detection policy and Scan Configuration, while a tenant profile is associated with a Cloud App Control policy rule.

quotes: The name of the SaaS application tenant that is displayed when configuring the DLP policy, Malware Detection policy, and Scan Configuration.
Policy Configured: The Data at Rest Scanning policies (DLP and Malware Detection) configured for the SaaS application tenant.
The name of the tenant profile that is displayed when configuring the Cloud App Control policy rule.

validation-code-ranges.title: Undefined tenant validation codes and whether they are the API errorCode
validation-code-ranges.detail: The validation error codes page defines codes 1, 2, 4, 201-299, 400-499, 500 and 501-599; codes 3, 5-200 and 300-399, and 600 and above, are not defined, and the page does not say these numbers are the `errorCode` values of the validation status response.

component-group-scope.title: Which applications support component site groups and how many groups a tenant may have
component-group-scope.detail: The component pages name only SharePoint as an example; the applications that support site groups and the number of groups a tenant may have are not stated, and the ServiceNow default object type list is not given.

reauth-effect.title: What a tenant needing reauthorization does to its scans and what triggers it
reauth-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "When `reAuth = true` on a tenant object, scans for that tenant will not run. This is triggered by expired or revoked OAuth tokens, a change in the SaaS application's OAuth policies, or administrative rotation of API credentials." No captured source states the effect on scans or lists the triggers. Resolve with a lab test of a tenant whose authorization is revoked.
reauth-effect.blocks: telling an operator whether scans are stopped while a tenant shows Reauthorization Required

oauth-scope.title: Whether the access Zscaler is granted to a SaaS tenant exceeds what scanning needs
oauth-scope.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The scope of that credential may be broader than the minimum necessary for scanning." The onboarding article lists the roles or permissions granted per application, but no source compares them with the minimum a scan needs.

gmail-trusted-domains.title: Whether Gmail tenants still treat external trusted domains and users as internal
gmail-trusted-domains.detail: The Adding SaaS Application Tenants article said, in its Gmail steps, that the Zscaler service views email addresses from the added external trusted domains, and the added trusted users, as trusted, internal users for Gmail. The capture of 2026-11-07 no longer has that text in the Gmail steps; the same two sentences remain for Exchange.
